Consult Summary:
- 48-year-old man with 3 days of watery diarrhea and prior brief vomiting, assessed as likely gastroenteritis; advised supportive care and follow-up if not improving.

History:
- Presenting complaint: watery diarrhea for approximately 3 days.
- Onset/duration/progression: started ~3 days ago with a few episodes of vomiting that have now resolved; diarrhea has continued 5–6 times/day and is watery.
- Associated symptoms: subjective weakness, decreased appetite, feeling dehydrated due to inability to retain fluids; felt mildly febrile at onset but currently feels “kind of fine.”
- Pertinent negatives: no visible blood in stool, no significant abdominal pain, no headache or muscle pains reported.
- Past medical history: asthma.
- Current medications: blue inhaler (name not specified) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: none reported.
- Family history: father died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago; mother has type 2 diabetes.
- Social history / preventive care: lives alone; software engineer; currently off work for the past 3 days; drinks alcohol infrequently; non-smoker.

Examination:

( no physical examination findings or vital signs documented )

Impression:
- Probable acute gastroenteritis (tummy bug).

Plan:
- Supportive management: oral rehydration emphasized; advised to drink plenty of fluids.
- Recommend oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Symptomatic treatment: Paracetamol suggested if feverish/weak — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Occupational advice: remain off work; advised to be diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours before returning to work.
- Follow-up: if symptoms persist or not improved by one week, return for reassessment; patient advised to call back sooner if condition worsens.
- No investigations or prescriptions documented during this consult.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, temperature, respiratory rate), abdominal examination findings, hydration status assessment, stool testing guidance (e.g., stool culture or testing) if clinically indicated, explicit review of current regular medications beyond inhaler, specific dosing instructions for recommended treatments (Dioralyte, paracetamol).
- Internal conflicts from transcript: none identified.
- Transcript quality comment: audio contains occasional pauses and repetitions but content is intelligible; no critical information appears obscured.
